item.title: Confluence tips
item.description:
A few practical notes to help you get the most out of PageMailer when preparing content in Confluence intended to be sent as an email.

Turn rich links into regular links

When pasting a link into a Confluence page, it will sometimes be turned into a rich link (or inline card in Atlassian terms). PageMailer will be able to process most of these links when they are public or when they are links to other Confluence pages and blogs, but other Atlassian links such as Jira, Trello, StatusPage, etc. are not currently supported (see our roadmap for future support).

item.title: Supported macros
item.description:
List of supported Confluence macros

The style of Confluence pages is matched in most templates. Note that some templates override this style to change the default font or re-style panels (e.g. by removing the icon), and more.

Macro Preview
Text, paragraphs and basic formatting
Lists
User mentions (links to user profile)
Task list
Blockquote
Headings
Date
Panels (all colors and types supported)
Code block
Decision list
Emojis
Images (with optional caption support, see image processing for more details)
Layouts (using /layout)
Horizontal rule
Status
Table (supports column split/merge and background colors)
Inline cards (rich links)
Block & embed cards (expanded links)
Expand (displays as open/expand in the email)
Files (icon and name shown inline, and the file is added as attachment to the email)

List of unsupported Confluence macros

We may eventually add support for some of what is detailed below, and we encourage you to check out our roadmap and share your feedback to help us prioritize future changes.

item.title: Image processing
item.description:
Upon processing Confluence pages to generate an email or when uploading logos, PageMailer processes images through our first-party API, which is hosted and owned by PageMailer. This API handles:

  • Compression of JPEG, PNG, and GIF files to reduce file size while maintaining quality.
  • Conversion of SVG files to PNG format for consistent rendering across email clients.
  • Resizing of images that exceed a certain width to ensure optimal display and reducing file size.

All image processing is performed securely and in accordance with our Privacy Policy. No third-party services are used for these operations, and your data remains within PageMailer’s or Atlassian’s infrastructure.
